# PB-02 operating-envelope measurement

PB-02 completes the measurement task with **negative performance acceptance**.
There is no supported normal operating envelope under the provisional budgets
from these experiments. In particular, the five-artifact workload misses 25 ms
p95 durable event admission even with no retained run history. Passing finite
points in the reduced profile do not establish a steady combined workload or a
500-agent product capacity claim. PB-03/PB-04 and later PERF-01 remain release
blocks; no limits were raised and no engine optimization was made here.

[Machine-readable evidence](PB-02.json), [raw timing vectors and configurations](PB-02.results.json),
[source reconciliation](PB-02.source-reconciliation.json), and the
[scoped optimization proposals](PB-02.optimizations.md) accompany this report.
Retained source archives, hashes, build/test logs and failed attempts are in
`/home/jkern/dev/.aq-qualification/pb02-2026-10-31/`. Verify its `SHA256SUMS`.

## Exact source and checks

Measured engine source is committed
`911fc5dc7d509688a078ff1715eda715b0b81cf1` (`b2cbf71` implementation plus the host
integration documentation commit), with the separately inventoried benchmark.
PB-01's retained bundle commit `921208a780e39c9d4cb68d5970d4f37b1e7a956b` is
**different**: 23 existing files differ and `runner/src/metrics.rs` was added.
Changes include sensitive-event fields, named join behavior, metrics and
index/storage/retention work, rather than just formatting. PB-01's earlier tests
therefore do not automatically qualify this source.

The current candidate passed 116 database-free tests, 22 explicitly enabled
PostgreSQL tests and 2 administrative CLI tests, strict workspace Clippy and
format checks. PostgreSQL correctness tests also used a fresh container pinned
to the measured image. New benchmark-only fixture validation and lint failures
were corrected before the final checks; their logs/observations are retained.
Existing engine source, the preexisting modified specification and PB-01 evidence
were not edited by this task.

Each final experiment retains its exact measured source archive, source inventory
and release executable hash. The public harness's later changes only clarify
full/minimal configuration-header labels and express the same debug-build refusal
without a Clippy constant-assert warning. These changes do not substitute a new
engine or a different measured release execution path. Rebuild from the retained
experiment archive for an exact measurement-source replay.

## Hardware and workload

The shared development host was an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, 12 cores/24 logical CPUs,
WSL2 x86_64 Linux 6.18.33.2, with Docker Desktop exposing 24 CPUs and about 31 GiB
RAM. Rust/cargo were 1.96.1, using release thin LTO. This was not an isolated
benchmark machine: other component compilation/testing could run concurrently.
Per-run load averages and toolchain/hardware details are retained; reduced runs
observed one-minute host load averages up to 8.48.

Every database was a new disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 Alpine container, pinned to
`postgres@sha256:266d3c257594e195b309ae9d1805e54c788f1d7b375f56bf6c367aac6c917e7b`,
limited to 2 CPUs and 1 GiB, with 128 MiB shared buffers and 32 connections.
`fsync`, `synchronous_commit` and `full_page_writes` were on. Connections used a
dynamic loopback TCP port. No production database, named volume, AQ service,
provider or hosted credential was used. The wrapper requires its fresh database
marker and removes only its uniquely named container/anonymous data volume.

The full profile uses five installed artifacts, three scopes, null run input,
128-byte event payloads, return-only roots and a wait/call pair for owned children.
For each starting size, real MemoryStorage admissions/transitions/events construct
fully indexed, settled state. One public Storage CAS imports that state into a
fresh namespace outside the measured window. This measures operation cost at
history sizes, not historical setup throughput. All namespace/default resource
limits remain unchanged. Full phases have 24 timing samples; p95 is nearest rank.

## Growing settled history

Each row starts with the indicated number of completed roots **and** retained
no-consumer events. Receipts are twice the root count. The event phase admits 24
more events without deleting history. Times below are the final full run; the
first full experiment is retained separately.

| Initial roots/events | Initial receipts | Final canonical state | Event p95 | Store load p95 | Store commit p95 | MemoryStorage event p95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 / 0 | 0 | 42,180 B | 28.798 ms | 4.156 ms | 24.649 ms | 0.359 ms |
| 32 / 32 | 64 | 117,035 B | 34.941 ms | 4.909 ms | 29.544 ms | 0.979 ms |
| 128 / 128 | 256 | 342,731 B | 56.690 ms | 8.440 ms | 46.067 ms | 2.890 ms |
| 512 / 512 | 1,024 | 1,250,342 B | 172.370 ms | 23.276 ms | 131.103 ms | 10.938 ms |

Load and commit quantiles are separate distributions and must not be added as if
they belonged to the same percentile sample. Instrumented transition closures
remain 0.065–0.093 ms p95, but exclude index synchronization and whole-state quota
serialization. Pairwise total wall minus load/commit is approximately 0.441,
1.040, 3.219 and 15.995 ms p95 across these sizes. Thus closure timing alone does
not establish a 1 ms total transition-CPU budget.

Storage remains synchronous and includes local TCP, JSON decoding/serialization,
SQL/index work and commit durability. It must stay off asynchronous authority,
renewal and cancellation handlers. Index discovery alone does not remove the
whole-snapshot cost.

## Pending children, queues and admission

With 0/8/32/128 unresolved owned children, event admission p95 is
31.340/34.711/42.079/82.133 ms. Children remain unresolved throughout the event
measurements; the benchmark does not discard or complete them to reduce load.
These are separate finite pending-child scenarios, not a combined maximum of all
history/backlog axes.

Three-scope ready queues serve `a,b,c` round robin while all three have work, then
continue remaining work. All tested equal prefixes passed. This establishes the
observed finite scope order, not a time-fair admission guarantee for arbitrary
producers. Queues were deliberately filled before dispatching:

| Starting history | Six ready roots: dispatch-call p95 | 24 ready roots: dispatch-call p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 39.688 ms | 40.423 ms |
| 32 | 45.464 ms | 45.929 ms |
| 128 | 68.833 ms | 73.938 ms |
| 512 | 170.025 ms | 186.270 ms |

At 512 history, dispatch-call p95 fails the 100 ms budget. Admission-to-first-visit
upper bounds are larger: the batch workload deliberately pauses service while
admitting the rest of the batch, and those wall times include that delay. They
are retained separately rather than conflated with dispatch-call latency.

Concurrent closed-loop admission uses 1/2/4 threads, eight requests each and at
most eight immediate CAS attempts per request. In the final run, 8/8, 15/16 and
30/32 requests complete; p95 request latency is 28.993, 296.068 and 418.530 ms.
The first run's four-thread result is 27/32, also retained. Refusals are explicit;
producer retry responsibility is not dropped or replaced with unbounded retries.
The synchronous connection mutex and optimistic namespace CAS do not establish
fair producer admission. A future AQ embedding needs a declared bounded ingress
policy in addition to fair ready-work discovery.

## Reduced finite profile and resource bounds

The separately declared reduced profile installs one artifact, uses a single
scope, 0/1/8/32 starting settled roots/events and ready backlogs 1/3. Each event cell
has 64 samples; each queue cell has 24 fresh namespace batches, two repetitions.
The entire reduced experiment is repeated in a second fresh container. Its
explicit smaller quotas are 35 runs, 96 events, 70 receipts, one queued destination
and 256 KiB canonical state.

Several small cells pass: event p95 at starting history 0/1 is 16.559–22.828 ms
across both final runs, and corresponding one-ready-root batches stay below
100 ms. Larger cells do not pass consistently: an eight-history event cell reaches
28.471 ms; 32-history cells reach 103.424 ms; a three-ready-root cell reaches
288.003 ms admission-to-first-visit. All results and outliers remain in the data.
Separate passing event-growth and queue points are not a measured combined,
steady operating envelope. These smaller quotas are experiment controls, not
recommended deployment limits or a workaround for the failed normal profile.

All five quota dimensions—runs, events, receipts, canonical state bytes and queued
destinations—refuse excess work while the canonical persisted state remains
identical. An already accepted queued destination is preserved. Default namespace
ceilings (10,000 runs, 100,000 events, 10,000 queued destinations, 1,000,000 receipts,
64 MiB) are **admission limits, not measured capacity**. No near-default-ceiling
performance or completion/control headroom claim is made. State-byte quotas are
not process heap limits.

The full runner peaks at 37,820 KiB RSS in this experiment; the reduced runs peak
near 10 MiB. The final full database is about 62 MB, with 4,548 committed and 53
rolled-back transactions, including setup/probes. Its final Docker memory sample
is 92.76 MiB under the declared 1 GiB limit; that is not a continuous peak-memory
measurement. Docker reports roughly 302 MB written across the full experiment.
These are measured resource costs, not a linear scale or 500-agent extrapolation.

## Reproduction and disposition

From the retained exact source, or the reviewed public harness:

```
crates/aq-playbooks-postgres/scripts/benchmark-envelope.sh .local/pb02/replay-full full
crates/aq-playbooks-postgres/scripts/benchmark-envelope.sh .local/pb02/replay-minimal minimal
```

The script builds the release example, validates fixtures before starting the
container, records source/hardware/durability settings and raw timings, and
refuses to overwrite existing results. Ordinary correctness tests remain
separate from these explicit performance experiments.

PB-03 targets repeated immutable-artifact work in PostgreSQL CAS; PB-04 targets
history-sensitive full-state transition persistence. Their correctness obligations
are detailed in the linked proposal, and the implementation graph records them
in commit `59028ed`, with PB-04 blocking PERF-01. PB-02 does not implement those
optimizations or pass broader performance acceptance. Protected-store performance,
production AQ adapters, open-loop sustained throughput and the assembled product
must be qualified separately.
